## Selected Species Information

This table provides the Primary Biological Features (PBFs) for the selected species.

```{r species-table, echo=FALSE, ft.align="left"}
# 0. load in PBF data
#PBFs <- read.csv("data/PBFs for Shiny app test.csv")
PBFs <- read.csv("C:/Users/elizabeth.keller/Documents/GitHub/PBF-Shiny-app/data/All PBFs - Stressor Categories.csv") # updated file

# data wrangling to make it the right format
# creates species+ESU/DPS; no separator if no ESU/DPS
PBFs$Species_full <- ifelse(
  is.na(PBFs$ESU_DPS) | PBFs$ESU_DPS == "",
  PBFs$Species,
  paste0(PBFs$Species, " – ", PBFs$ESU_DPS)
)
# Sort the PBFs data frame alphabetically by Species_full
PBFs <- PBFs[order(PBFs$Species_full), ]

# 1. Ensure data and species are defined inside the chunk
selected_species <- c("Atlantic Salmon – Gulf of Maine DPS",
                      "Atlantic Sturgeon – Carolina DPS", 
                      "Atlantic Sturgeon – Chesapeake Bay DPS")

# 2. Group PBFs into a list
final_table <- PBFs %>%
  filter(Species_full %in% selected_species) %>%
  group_by(Species_full) %>%
  summarize(PBF_list = list(unique(PBF)), .groups = "drop")

# 3. Build the table using as_bullet()
ft <- flextable(final_table) %>%
  compose(
    j = "PBF_list",
    value = as_paragraph(as_bullet(PBF_list))
  ) %>%
  # Styling
  set_header_labels(Species_full = "Species", PBF_list = "PBF") %>%
  theme_vanilla() %>%
  autofit() %>%
  valign(j = "PBF_list", valign = "top")

# Display the table
ft
```
